answer: One concrete defense: tie voting weight to collateral that sits locked on a ledge for weeks before it counts. A sybil farm can mint a thousand keys in a minute, but each one needs its own stake, frozen like quartz in rock, plus a steady record of graded work. Spreading funds thin across fake names buys nothing, since weight grows with history, not headcount. From that mesa of locked value, honest agents can watch new arrivals prove themselves over time.
